item.title: How Your Brain Knows It’s Cold
item.description: How do we feel the frost? Scientists have captured the first atomic-level images of the body’s "cold sensor" in action, revealing how menthol tricks our brain.

item.title: OCD Brains Work Harder to Stay on Track
item.description: It’s not just a repetitive thought—it’s a brain working overtime. New research shows why the OCD brain recruits extra regions just to keep track of daily sequences.

item.title: How the Brain Knows When to Stop Scratching an Itch
item.description: Ever wondered why you stop scratching? Scientists have found the nervous system's internal "brake" that tells your brain when you've scratched enough.

item.title: Mounjaro’s Active Ingredient Slashes Alcohol Intake
item.description: From weight loss to sobriety. New research reveals how the active ingredient in Mounjaro "mutes" the brain's reward system to slash alcohol cravings.

item.title: Hidden Cause of Permanent Hearing Loss Identified
item.description: It’s not just about the volume. Scientists discover the "death flip" in cell membranes that causes permanent hearing loss and why certain drugs trigger it.

item.title: Could an “Exercise Pill” Help Treat Depression?
item.description: Exercise is medicine, but what if you can't take the dose? Scientists explore "exercise mimetics"—pills that trick your brain into thinking you've just finished a workout.

item.title: New Bio-Implant for Spinal Cord Repair
item.description: Muting the "brake" on repair. Scientists develop a 3D-printed spinal implant that uses RNA to trigger nerve regrowth and bridge the gap of paralysis.

item.title: Predicting Autism Traits Through Infant Sleep
item.description: Quiet isn't always enough. Scientists discover that babies with sensory sensitivity stay "tethered" to the outside world, resulting in shallower, less restorative sleep.

item.title: Uncanny Average: Most People Can No Longer Spot an AI Face
item.description: Think you can spot a fake? Think again. Scientists reveal that the most realistic AI faces aren't given away by what's wrong with them, but by what's "too right."

item.title: Prenatal Lead Exposure Affects the Aging Brain
item.description: A biological time capsule reveals a 60-year secret. Scientists find that lead exposure in the womb can act as a "cognitive accelerator," adding years to the aging brain.
